I independently ran `node tools/run-code.mjs` on this file three more times in isolation (no other process involved): exit 1, exit 1, exit 0. The `id=killed` block (line 705) fails about two-thirds of the time because xUnit v3 does not guarantee the execution order of `Classify_BelowThreshold_ReturnsFreezing` vs `Classify_AboveThreshold_ReturnsNotFreezing` inside `FreezingTests`, and the article's literal expected output hard-codes one specific order. This is a real, reproducible flakiness in the article's code, not a fluke of this session or a race with another agent's process, and it is independent of my design/UX score below, which covers only rendering, layout and readability per my rubric. Screenshots read: all 12 desktop-light parts + fold, all 18 mobile-dark parts + fold, desktop-dark fold + parts 01/06/11, mobile-light fold + parts 01/07/10/14.
justification: This is one of the strongest-rendering pages in the pillar and clearly beats both comparison pages on presentation. Microsoft Learn's own code-coverage article is plain prose and single-language code blocks with one embedded screenshot and no dark mode; Codecov's blog is a marketing page with a hero image, share buttons and a static truth table. This article instead opens on a runnable, falsifiable claim, alternates code/output/prose in short beats, and never runs more than a few sentences without a code block, callout or the one figure. Heading hierarchy is a clean, specific H2/H3 outline that matches the desktop 'On this page' TOC exactly. The single SVG diagram (two stacked number lines, boundary point highlighted) is genuinely informative rather than decorative, is fully theme-correct (the boundary dot remaps from a saturated red in light mode to a legible coral/pink in dark mode via `d-fill-bad`, no hard-coded colors), stays within the 360-wide phone budget with annotations placed under each line as the guide asks, and its caption states exactly what to notice. Callouts (one `:::note` on toolchain provenance, four `:::exercise` blocks) are restrained, visually distinct in both themes, and use collapsed `<details>`-style solutions so exercises are not given away — exercise 1's solution correctly nests its code+output inside the collapsed block rather than showing it above the fold. Output panels consistently keep the operative comparison values (`Expected:`/`Actual:`, `Line coverage:`, `Branch coverage:`) within the visible ~40 columns on a 390px phone; only trailing, non-essential fields (`Skipped:`, `Not Run:`, `Time:`) fall into the scroll fade, which matches the site's own documented trade-off rather than violating it. Sources are both listed in the footer and hyperlinked inline at the point of every citation (an issue the binary-search review flagged that this article does not repeat). Byline, dates, reading time, breadcrumbs, prev/next, three related-by-tag articles and the 'Keep reading' block all render correctly in all four theme/device combinations, and `docs/crosslinks/testing/code-coverage.md` correctly documents why no planned-but-unpublished links were needed. The two things keeping this off a 9+: long xUnit test method names (`Classify_AtThreshold_ReturnsFreezing`, `Classify_AboveThreshold_ReturnsNotFreezing`) run past the 390px fold in both the code blocks and the OUTPUT panels for every `FreezingTests`/`HeatAdvisoryTests` example from 'What a branch adds' onward, and the run-code flakiness documented above and in the first issue below, which is a correctness/harness concern rather than a rendering one but is severe enough that the page cannot ship until it is fixed regardless of any critic's score.

issues.location: id=killed block, lines 705-730 (`FreezingTests` with two `[Fact]`s asserting a combined, order-sensitive console transcript)
issues.problem: xUnit v3 does not guarantee the order in which `[Fact]` methods inside one test class run. The article's expected output for this block hard-codes `Classify_BelowThreshold_ReturnsFreezing` failing before `Classify_AboveThreshold_ReturnsNotFreezing`. Three independent, isolated runs of `node tools/run-code.mjs src/content/articles/testing/code-coverage.md` on this machine produced exit 1, exit 1, exit 0 — the block genuinely fails about two-thirds of the time because the runner picks the other order and the diff-checked stdout no longer matches. `docs/ARTICLES_PLAN.md` definition of done item 4 requires run-code to be green, and it is not reliably green today; the gate.json snapshot showing `runCode.pass: true` simply happened to land on the lucky third of the time.
issues.fixLooksLike: Make the block order-independent: split it into two separate single-fact `csharp run` blocks (as the rest of the article already does for `weak`/`tight`/`fixed`/`boundary`), or add an explicit xUnit test-collection/method orderer so the two facts always run in the order the prose describes, or rewrite the surrounding prose so it describes each failure's cause without asserting a specific combined ordering, then re-run `node tools/run-code.mjs` several times in a row to confirm it is no longer flaky before handing off.
